pattern_identified.conclusion: Option extraction code treats letter labels in diagrams/statements as option markers, splitting on (A), (B), (C), (D) when actual options are numbered (1), (2), (3), (4). This causes completely wrong option extraction.

technical_root_cause.issue: Function searches for option families (ABCD or 1234) and splits text on first complete family found. For questions with letter labels in diagrams/statements, it incorrectly identifies (A), (B), (C), (D) as options when actual options are (1), (2), (3), (4).
technical_root_cause.code_snippet:
for family in ('ABCD','1234'):
    pattern=re.compile(r'\((['+family+r'])\)|(?<!\w)(['+family+r'])[.)]\s')
    matches=list(pattern.finditer(text))
    # ... finds ABCD first, treats as options
technical_root_cause.problem: Function prioritizes ABCD family over 1234 family. When both exist (letter labels in text + numbered options), it incorrectly chooses ABCD as options.
technical_root_cause.fix_needed: Modify choose_options() to prefer numbered options (1234) when both letter labels and numbered options exist, or detect when letters are diagram labels vs option markers

conclusion: ✅ CRITICAL BUG IDENTIFIED - Questions Q37/51/56/60/67/70 with lettered diagrams have INCORRECT OPTIONS extracted. Letter labels (A,B,C,D) in diagrams/statements are being treated as option markers when actual options are numbered (1,2,3,4).
